1. Points of the segment. For τ ∈ [0, 1], ‖τv‖ = τ‖v‖ ≤ ‖v‖ < R, so τv ∈ ball(0, R).

2. Regularity. ball(0, R) is open and h is C² on it. So at every point p of the ball:
- h is differentiable at p with derivative fderiv ℝ h p (ContDiffOn.differentiableOn, DifferentiableOn.differentiableAt);
- fderiv ℝ h is C¹ on the ball (ContDiffOn.fderiv_of_isOpen), hence differentiable at p with derivative fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ h) p.

3. One-variable derivatives. Let φ(τ) := h(τv) and φ₁(τ) := Dh(τv)v = fderiv ℝ h (τ • v) v. Let τ ∈ [0, 1].
- The chain rule along the line τ ↦ τv, whose derivative is v (HasFDerivAt.comp_hasDerivAt), gives φ'(τ) = Dh(τv)v = φ₁(τ).
- The derivative of evaluation at the fixed vector v (HasDerivAt.clm_apply with a constant) gives φ₁'(τ) = fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ h) (τv) v v = D²h(τv)(v, v), by iteratedFDeriv_two_apply.

4. First-derivative bound. Let τ ∈ [0, 1]. Every point of [0, τ] lies in [0, 1], where |φ₁'| ≤ S by hypothesis. The mean value inequality for φ₁ on [0, τ] (norm_image_sub_le_of_norm_deriv_le_segment') gives |φ₁(τ) − φ₁(0)| ≤ S·τ.

5. Remainder. Let ψ(τ) := φ(τ) − φ(0) − τ·φ₁(0). Then ψ(0) = 0 and ψ'(τ) = φ₁(τ) − φ₁(0) on [0, 1], so |ψ'(τ)| ≤ Sτ by step 4. Let β(τ) := Sτ²/2, so β(0) = 0 and β'(τ) = Sτ. Since ‖ψ(0)‖ ≤ β(0) and ‖ψ'(τ)‖ ≤ β'(τ) for τ ∈ [0, 1), comparison (image_norm_le_of_norm_deriv_right_le_deriv_boundary) gives |ψ(τ)| ≤ β(τ) for τ ∈ [0, 1]. In particular |ψ(1)| ≤ S/2. Equivalently, |ψ(1)| = |∫₀¹ ψ'| ≤ ∫₀¹ Sτ dτ = S/2, as in the parent proof.

6. Since 1·v = v and 0·v = 0, ψ(1) = h(v) − h(0) − Dh(0)v. Hence |h(v) − h(0) − Dh(0)v| ≤ S/2. ∎
